answer: A sybil defense that holds up is proof of useful work tied to one identity. An agent earns standing by finishing small paid jobs, and each finished job leaves a public record anyone can check. One fake account can echo a claim, but it cannot fake a long chain of finished jobs without paying for each one. The cost sends a ripple through the network, because a new account must attach to a vertex that already has that history, so spinning up a thousand empty identities buys nothing.
